skill.name: global-validation
skill.description: Provides guidance for secure input validation across forms, APIs, services, and background jobs. It emphasizes allowlists, type checks, sanitization, clear errors, and server-side enforcement.
skill.summary: Guide secure server-side validation across application entry points.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: Two static findings are false positives: markdown code formatting and a business validation example. The parent-directory markdown link is confirmed because it directs use of a file outside the packaged skill boundary.

remediation.suggestion: Package the referenced validation guidance inside the skill, or replace the parent-directory link with inline instructions.

static_findings.snippet: - When creating form request classes in `app/Http/Requests/` for validation logic
- When implementing business rule validation (e.g., sufficient balance, valid date ranges)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 contains markdown inline code for a Laravel directory path, not Ruby backtick execution. There is no command invocation or dynamic shell input.

Line 28 links to ../../../agent-os/standards/global/validation.md outside the skill directory, and line 27 instructs readers to use it. This can cause out-of-package file access and makes marketplace review incomplete.
Line 20 describes business rule validation examples, such as balances and date ranges. It does not request system inventory, host discovery, or sensitive environment inspection.

content.value_statement: Input validation gaps create security, data quality, and user experience problems. This skill guides secure validation rules, sanitization, error messages, and consistency across entry points.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of server-side validation for forms, APIs, controllers, services, and background jobs.
Encourages allowlist-based rules for accepted types, formats, ranges, and required fields.
Covers input sanitization concerns for SQL injection, XSS, and command injection.
Promotes specific validation error messages that help users correct invalid input.
Includes validation considerations for file uploads, custom validators, and business rules.
limitations: The packaged skill is brief and delegates detailed standards to an external relative file.
It does not include ready-to-run validation code or tests.
It does not define framework-specific rule syntax beyond the Laravel request path example.
It cannot replace threat modeling, security testing, or product-specific business rule review.

use_cases.title: Secure API Input
use_cases.description: Design validation for request payloads before controller, service, or persistence logic uses submitted data.

use_cases.title: Improve Form Validation
use_cases.description: Add clear server-side rules and user-facing messages while keeping client-side checks as a usability layer.

use_cases.title: Standardize Validation Reviews
use_cases.description: Review validation coverage across forms, APIs, uploads, custom validators, and background jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-validation to add server-side validation for this form. Include required fields, type checks, allowlists, and clear error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Validate API Input
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-validation to validate this API endpoint. Cover payload shape, allowed values, ranges, sanitization needs, and failure messages.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-validation to review these validation rules. Identify missing server-side checks, weak allowlists, vague errors, and unvalidated entry points.

prompt_templates.title: Design Validation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-validation to design a validation plan for forms, APIs, uploads, background jobs, and business rules in this feature.

output: Required name, email, password, and consent fields are checked on the server.
Email format and password length rules are explicit.
Each failure message explains the specific field problem.

output_examples.input: Review validation for a file upload endpoint.
output: Allowed file types, maximum size, and required metadata are defined.
Server-side checks run before storage or processing.
Error messages tell users which upload rule failed.

output_examples.input: Plan validation for a payment transfer request.
output: Amount, currency, account identifiers, and date ranges are validated.
Business rules check available balance and transfer limits.
Invalid requests fail before any account state changes.

best_practices: Apply validation on the server for every entry point, even when client-side checks exist.
Use allowlists for accepted values, file types, formats, and ranges.
Write specific error messages that help users fix one field at a time.
anti_patterns: Relying only on client-side validation for security decisions.
Accepting broad free-form values when a defined allowlist is possible.
Returning vague validation errors that hide which field failed.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a validation library?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance for adding and reviewing validation in application code.

faq.question: Does it enforce validation automatically?
faq.answer: No. You still need to implement rules, sanitization, error handling, and tests in your project.

faq.question: Can it help with Laravel projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill mentions form request classes and general validation across controllers, services, and APIs.

faq.question: Does it cover sanitization?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes sanitization concerns for SQL injection, XSS, and command injection.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publishing?
faq.answer: They should package the referenced standards or replace the parent-directory link with inline guidance.
